header.running_head: Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Refuses to Accept wealth given to him

blocks.text: ﷺ invited him to accept Islaam but he refused. Rasulullaah ﷺ therefore said, "I do not accept the gift of a Mushrik."[^1]

Another narration from Hadhrat Ayaadh bin Himaar Mujaashi'ee (RA) states that when he once presented to Rasulullaah ﷺ a camel or something else as a gift, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him whether he was a Muslim. When he replied in the negative, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I have been prohibited from accepting gifts from Mushrikeen."[^2]
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Refuses to Accept wealth given to him
He Refuses to Accept his Allowance from the Baytul Maal

Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once addressed the people. After praising Allaah, he said, "Verily the best of all intelligence is Taqwa." The narration continues to the point where it states that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was proceeding to the marketplace early next morning when Hadhrat Umar (RA) (met him and) asked, "Where are you off to?" When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) informed him that he was on his way to the marketplace, Hadhrat Umar (RA) remarked, "You have been appointed to a post that will preoccupy you from any engagements at the marketplace." "Subhaanallaah!" exclaimed Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), "Will it preoccupy me from (providing for) my family?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "We shall fix a reasonable allowance for you." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) remarked, "Woe to you, O Umar! I fear that it may not be permissible for me to take anything from that wealth." (By consultation with the other Sahabah (RA), an allowance was fixed for Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA))

During his period of just over two years, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used eight thousand Dirhams (from the Baytul Maal). On his deathbed, he said, "I had mentioned to Umar that I fear that it may not be permissible for me to take anything from that wealth but he overpowered me. Now that I am dying, I want you to take eight thousand Dirhams from my estate and deposit it in the Baytul Maal." When this money was brought to Hadhrat Umar (RA), he said, "May Allaah shower His mercy on Abu Bakr (RA). He has certainly exhausted those to come after him."[^3]
The Incident Between him and Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA)

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Umar
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Umar narrates that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) came to (her father) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) when he was ill and about to breathe his last. She recited a couplet (which means)
"By your life! Prosperity is of no benefit to the youth
Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.177).
Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, Ibn Jareer and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.177).
